overall: The AG found the Methuen City Council did not violate the Open Meeting Law by meeting in executive session under Purpose 4 to discuss school security; the later claim about withholding contracts was declined as not in the original complaint and is a Public Records matter.

allegations.summary: Council allegedly entered executive session on Nov 7, 2022 for an improper purpose, citing Exemption 4 to discuss security contracts for school buildings.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the discussions during the executive session meeting held on November 7, 2022, were appropriate under Purpose 4 as they related to the security of the City’s schools and the safety of teachers and students in those schools.

allegations.summary: Complainant later suggested the Council used executive session to illegally withhold the two security contracts and related procurement records from the public.
allegations.key_passage: we decline to review an allegation that was not included within the original complaint to the Council because the Council has not had an opportunity to respond to it.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
